text: You met Genie Code's premise back in Lesson 35 — unlike a generic coding assistant, it operates with full context of your schema, lineage, and governance. Genie products have grown over ten times in the past year and are used by 90% of Databricks customers. This is broadly adopted production tooling, not a lab demo.

Real data and ML work rarely fits in a single prompt — it spans notebooks, SQL, pipelines, dashboards, jobs, and models at once. At Summit 2026, Genie Code moved from a small side panel to a full-page command center managing multiple concurrent threads, each scoped to a different asset. Scheduled tasks, coming soon, let it run on your behalf overnight, creating a thread with results for you to review when you return.

What makes Genie Code's advice trustworthy rather than generic comes from two places. Databricks itself — a decade-plus of running production ML, encoding lessons like correcting for class imbalance automatically. And your team's own Genie Ontology — learning how your team actually builds features, trains models, and evaluates candidates, instead of falling back on irrelevant defaults.

Genie ZeroOps, entering private preview, is the autonomous background agent that operates for you. Detect catches even silent failures through continuous monitoring. Assess uses Unity Catalog lineage to trace a failure to its real root cause. Remediate generates a fix using your real development workflow as context. And Verify runs that fix in a sandbox against zero-copy clones of real data — never production — with nothing applied until a human approves.

That's this entire course, start to finish — from Unity Catalog governance and Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines through performance tuning, security, and now the agentic capabilities that help you author and operate every pipeline you've built. You're ready for production Databricks work at an advanced level.
